{{more citations needed|date=January 2019}}
A sinusoidal waveform is said to have a '''unity amplitude''' when the amplitude of the wave is equal to 1.

<math>x(t) = a \sin(\theta(t))</math>

where <math>a = 1</math>. This terminology is most commonly used in [[digital signal processing]] and is usually associated with the [[Fourier series]] and [[Fourier transform]] sinusoids that involve a [[duty cycle]], <math>\alpha</math>, and a defined [[fundamental period]], <math>T_o</math>.

Analytic signals with unit amplitude satisfy the [[Bedrosian theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Huang |first=Norden E. |last2=Wu |first2=Zhaohua |last3=Long |first3=Steven R. |last4=Arnold |first4=Kenneth C. |last5=Chen |first5=Xianyao |last6=Blank |first6=Karin |date=2009 |title=On Instantaneous Frequency |url=http://rcada.ncu.edu.tw/2009%20Vol.1_No.2/1.ON%20INSTANTANEOUS%20FREQUENCY.pdf |url-status=dead |journal=Advances in Adaptive Data Analysis |language=en |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=177–229 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171016175102/http://rcada.ncu.edu.tw/2009%20Vol.1_No.2/1.ON%20INSTANTANEOUS%20FREQUENCY.pdf |archive-date=2017-10-16}}</ref>
